rationale:
WHAT THIS IS. bugs_closed/314 fixed the council gate so it could see that a DB migration is config, not prose. It closed 2026-08-20 naming two residuals. This is the second, quoted from its own banner: "A FOURTH copy of the migration vocabulary exists and is already drifted: scripts/pattern-check.py:384-385 ... A candidate for its own small ticket." 314 stays closed; this is that ticket. It is admitted without FORCE=1 only because scripts/pattern-check.py entered scope on 2026-08-24 — this lane's own August fix is what made its follow-up reviewable.

THE DEFECT. scripts/pattern-check.py runs from .githooks/pre-commit on every commit in every session. check_unguarded_migration_insert is the commit-time half of bugs_open/007 Class C: a migration whose INSERT carries no guard cannot be replayed, and a replay dies on a raw 23505 that reads as broken SQL — migration 151 blocked the runner 3 days. To run, it must first decide which changed files are migrations. It used ^\d{3}_[a-z0-9_]+\.sql$ — LOWERCASE ONLY — while the runner's appliable rule (run-migrations.sh:283 + SIDECAR_RE:65) accepts capitals. The file's own comment states the contract it was breaking (:378): "lint_idempotency in run-migrations.sh — SAME semantics, keep them in step".

Two failures, and the second is the one worth your attention. (1) COVERAGE: any appliable migration with a capital anywhere in its name was skipped, silently. (2) REASONING: the comment "# sidecars (_ROLLBACK etc.) excluded" was TRUE FOR THE WRONG REASON — sidecars were excluded only because they happen to be uppercase. A proxy standing in for a rule is 314's own defect class, and it is the SAME mistake your editquality seat caught INSIDE 314's fix (I had excluded _HOLD by reusing SIDECAR_RE, which answers "will --apply run this?", as a proxy for "is this the change?"). It was in this file the whole time.

⚠ A CORRECTION I AM MAKING TO 314'S OWN BANNER, AND IT CHANGED THE FIX. "Already drifted" is WRONG. git log -S on both files: the runner gained [A-Za-z] on 2026-07-20 (a51333fd7); this lint was written lowercase-only on 2026-07-25 (9d95e1c31), five days LATER. The two literals have NEVER matched — it was WRONG AT BIRTH, not drifted. That is not pedantry, it selects the remedy: I had already built and mutation-tested a drift guard modelled on council_scope_drift_warn() (read the runner, assert its lines have not moved), and against a birth defect THAT GUARD IS GREEN FOR EVER because the runner never moved. I would have shipped a watcher structurally incapable of catching the defect it was named after, with a passing mutation suite — because I had mutated the runner, the half that was always right. Thrown away and replaced; recorded in WRONG_CALLS.md and corrected in the 314 banner itself so the next reader does not inherit it.

MEASUREMENTS, all [MEASURED 2026-09-02] and dated because the corpus moved three times during this session (1,132 -> 1,140 -> 1,142 files; other lanes add migrations live). Appliable by the runner 743; visible to the pre-fix lint 738; blind spot 5: 482_ROLLBACK_claim_timeout_exclusion.sql (appliable — SIDECAR_RE anchors at the END, this name merely BEGINS with ROLLBACK) plus four _sibling_A_/_lever_B_ files. ALL FIVE ARE ALREADY DO-GUARDED, so this is a LATENT detector gap, NOT live damage — stated plainly rather than dressed up. The exposure is the next file of that shape carrying a bare INSERT. My first census of this said 660 and was wrong (comm(1), inputs its own collation rejected; it warned and I read past it). WRONG_CALLS.md.

THE DESIGN DECISION: _HOLD IS IN, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS THE SUBSTANTIVE CHANGE. Mirroring the runner's appliable set — the obvious fix — EXCLUDES _HOLD and writes the worst case out of the lint while looking rigorous. run-migrations.sh:245-250 REFUSES --record-only on any sidecar, so a _HOLD CANNOT be ledger-recorded while it carries the suffix; the house sequence is forced: hand-apply, RENAME, then record. [MEASURED] that promotion is routine — 26 distinct files renamed _HOLD -> plain between 2026-08-01 and 09-02, and I checked they STUCK rather than trusting git's rename inference: 26 of 26 on disk today under the plain name. Between rename and record the runner sees a pending, unrecorded, appliable file and REPLAYS it. So _HOLD is the one category GUARANTEED to be applied out of band before the ledger can know.

Timing follows: the lint fires at WRITE time, the only moment that satisfies its own stated purpose (:378, "at the moment the author can still add the guard"). One honest narrowing of my own claim: _HOLD promotions were ALREADY partly linted, at the rename commit — changed_files() uses --diff-filter=ACMR and a rename lists the lowercase destination. So what this adds for _HOLD is the write-time hit, when the SQL is actually being authored; the rename hit is a harmless second look that already existed.

BOUNDARY, so it is not blurred: coverage widens to _HOLD (a trailing uppercase suffix that IS the change) and NOT to _ROLLBACK (the undo), _VERIFY (assertions, no writes) or _SUPERSEDED (retired), which are hand-run against an already-decided state.

WHY NOT SINGLE-SOURCE IT WITH scripts/council-scope.sh, and please do not ask me to. That file enumerates the same three suffixes and today selects the same set, but answers a DIFFERENT question — "is this the change, for review?" — where this asks "could the runner ever replay it?". Collapsing two questions because their answers currently agree is exactly the defect 314 exists to remove, and you caught precisely that inside 314's fix. Derived independently, with the convergence written into the comment so it reads as deliberate.

THE GUARD. Four copies of this vocabulary exist: the runner (source of truth), council-scope.sh (watched), 098's SCOPE_PATHS (watched), and this one — unwatched, and the one that was wrong. Given the birth-defect finding, what is owed is not a change-watcher but a PARITY test comparing the two literals AND pinning the decisions in a must-lint/must-not-lint table. The realistic future regression is not the runner moving (8 commits ever touch it) — it is a session reading SIDECAR_RE, deciding the lint "disagrees", and reconciling it, silently dropping _HOLD. A literal-only check passes happily while the RULE is wrong; only the fixture table catches that. Proven by mutation, not asserted.

Placed in cmd/config-key-audit/ with three precedents doing exactly this shape (optional_budget_cron_parity_test.go, cron_parity_test.go, retention_parity_test.go), reached through the EXISTING scripts/lib/precommit-gotest.sh rather than a new mechanism — that helper exists because your reuse seat objected (corr be252395 r2) to two hand-rolled implementations of this shape in this same package, and a Python arm of my own would have earned that objection a third time.

NOT BUNDLED, STATED RATHER THAN OMITTED. The heads-up I sent the dispatch_throughput lane before touching files under them (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3) made them audit themselves and find SEVEN runner-appliable migrations applied by hand with zero ledger rows. They asked me to add a ledger census here. I declined and filed bugs_open/426: run-migrations.sh's DEFAULT dry run ALREADY computes that set (PENDING, :328-339) and already lints and probes it — the check exists, is free, is mandated by CLAUDE.md, and simply was not run. Adding a second census here would duplicate a working check AND create a fifth copy of this very vocabulary, in a script with no DB connection at commit time.

PROCESS. No 090 run, per the owner ruling of 2026-07-31's named escape hatch and for the reasons 314 §7 gave: the mechanism is two predicates read at source and one reproducible grep loop; nothing is inferred. No RFC: owner ruling 2026-07-29 §1 asks for one when a shared mechanism's GUARANTEES change — this corrects which files a detector covers to match its own stated contract and adds a test; the lint's contract, output shape, CHECKS interface and advisory status are unchanged. 2026-08-02 §2 does not apply: no new authority on a seam, and the check structurally cannot block (pre-commit wraps it `|| true`; main() try/excepts each check). Expect ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: point_fix.

plan.summary: Correct scripts/pattern-check.py's migration file predicate so the bugs_open/007 Class C idempotency lint covers every file the runner could ever replay — including _HOLD, the highest-risk category, which was excluded by an accident of letter case — and add the parity test the copy never had. The predicate was wrong at birth, not drifted, so the guard compares the two literals and pins the decisions rather than watching the runner for change. Advisory throughout; cannot block a commit. [MEASURED 2026-09-02] 0 new findings and 0 coverage lost on a 1,142-file corpus; all controls incl. disconfirming and mutation runs are in the risks block.

edits.rationale: Replace a lowercase-only pattern whose sidecar exclusion was an accident of case with an explicit two-part predicate: the runner's appliable-name rule VERBATIM, minus an ENUMERATION of the never-replayed suffixes. Enumeration rather than the runner's catch-all SIDECAR_RE so an unanticipated suffix (there is one live today: 668_terms_publish_RELOCK.sql) defaults to IN — a wasted advisory line, never a silent miss. _HOLD is therefore IN. Written [0-9]{3} not \d{3} so the parity test can assert byte equality rather than translate dialects. Comment block records the Q1/Q2/Q3 distinction, the birth-defect provenance with both shas, and an explicit instruction not to reconcile this to SIDECAR_RE.
edits.sketch:
-MIGRATION_NAME = re.compile(r"^\\d{3}_[a-z0-9_]+\\.sql$")   # sidecars (_ROLLBACK etc.) excluded
+# VERBATIM from run-migrations.sh:283. Change only together with the runner.
+MIGRATION_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9]{3}_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\\.sql$")
+MIGRATION_NEVER_REPLAYED_RE = re.compile(r"_(ROLLBACK|VERIFY|SUPERSEDED)[A-Z0-9_]*\\.sql$")
+
+
+def migration_is_lintable(name):
+    """Q3: could the runner ever execute this file's SQL on replay? (_HOLD: yes.)"""
+    return bool(MIGRATION_NAME_RE.match(name)) and not MIGRATION_NEVER_REPLAYED_RE.search(name)

 # call site:
-        if not MIGRATION_NAME.match(os.path.basename(path)):
+        if not migration_is_lintable(os.path.basename(path)):
             continue

edits.rationale: The guard. Pins three drift risks: (1) the copy is still the runner's, byte for byte, at BOTH paired sites; (2) every suffix the lint excludes is one the runner would refuse to apply, so the lint can never exempt a genuinely replayable file; (3) the DECISIONS, via a must-lint/must-not-lint table — the only test that catches a deliberate divergence being un-deliberated, i.e. a session reconciling the exclusion to SIDECAR_RE and dropping _HOLD. A fourth test runs the REAL Python function so a change to migration_is_lintable() that leaves the constants alone is still caught, and t.Skips (never silently passes) if python3 is absent. Extraction is anchored (?m)^ so a comment quoting the pattern cannot satisfy it.

Runs the parity test at the one moment the author is present, scoped to the two sources of the rule and the test itself. Third caller of the EXISTING scripts/lib/precommit-gotest.sh (which exists because the reuse seat objected to two hand-rolled copies of this shape here); relevance predicate and guidance stay in the caller, per that helper's stated split. Deliberately NOT scoped to the migrations directory: firing on ~20 migration commits/day would compile a package importing platform/orchestration/... on a tree that often does not build from another session's WIP, so most runs would print 'could not tell' and train authors to ignore it. Uses a -run filter against the helper's stated preference for '', because this package carries four unrelated parity suites and running them all would report another guard's real failure under this one's headline.

plan.risks:
RISK 1 — NOISE, the failure mode this file fears most. pattern-check.py's header says a false positive that blocks is a fleet-wide outage and that 'anything that fired on ordinary work was cut'. Widening a predicate is how noise gets added. MEASURED over the live 1,142-file corpus with the file's own exemption logic: 45 newly visible, 0 new findings, 0 coverage lost. Had it been non-zero I would be reporting those as latent 007 hazards rather than suppressing them. Residual risk is future files, which is the intent.

RISK 2 — I WIDENED PAST THE RUNNER'S OWN RULE, deliberately, and this is the objection I most expect. Including _HOLD means the predicate is NOT the runner's appliable set, so 'keep them in step' now means the NAME rule, not the whole predicate. Defensible only because the two answer different questions, which is now written into the file rather than left to be rediscovered — and pinned by fixture, so a future reconciliation to SIDECAR_RE fails loudly. If the council wants strict parity instead, say so explicitly, but note that strict parity re-excludes the one category guaranteed to be hand-applied before the ledger can know about it.

RISK 3 — THE PARITY TEST IS A SOURCE SCAN, so a reformat of either constant across lines fails with t.Fatalf('literal not found'). Loud, like its three precedents, and preferred to a silent pass. Extraction is anchored (?m)^ so a comment quoting the pattern cannot satisfy it — the estate has a landmine about exactly that vacuous-pass shape.

RISK 4 — A STAGED-DIFF GUARD CANNOT SEE PRE-EXISTING DRIFT. It fires when drift is introduced, not when it already sits at HEAD. That gap is real and measured elsewhere in this estate: RFC_022's parity test was found FAILING at HEAD for days (check-optional-key-parity.sh's own header). scripts/verify-head-builds.sh --test and any go test ./cmd/config-key-audit/ close it; nothing here does, and the caller's header says so rather than implying coverage it does not have. I considered scoping to the migrations directory to catch it at use time and rejected it — see edit 3's rationale.

RISK 5 — THE FILTER IS A ROSTER. precommit-gotest.sh's own docs prefer '' because a -run filter silently stops matching if a test is renamed. I used 'MigrationLint' anyway, because this package carries four unrelated parity suites and running them all would report ANOTHER guard's real failure under this one's headline — a confidently mis-attributed finding being worse than a narrow one. The roster risk is pinned by every test in the file starting TestMigrationLint. Say if you would rather have the trade the other way.

RISK 6 — A FIFTH COPY? The test file holds the runner's literal for comparison. It is a copy of the SOURCE OF TRUTH held to fail loudly when it stops matching, not an independent rule anything selects on — which is precisely what none of the four had.

RISK 7 — SAME-FILE PASSENGER. scripts/pattern-check.py has had 12 commits in 16 days from other lanes; a pathspec commit cannot exclude a same-file passenger. Re-checked git status immediately before committing; the file was clean and unmodified by others throughout.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE. The lint still cannot see a migration that is unguarded AND already applied out of band — that is bugs_open/426, filed separately, where the check already exists in the runner's dry run and is simply undriven. I have not touched 314's other residual (the 097/098 scripts' own out-of-scope status), because nobody has asked and it is a judgement call rather than a defect.

REVERSIBILITY. Advisory scripts read from the tree at invocation — no image, no tag, no roll. Live on commit; reverting is one commit and takes effect on the next commit anyone makes. 314's 'verify against the running pod' caveat does not transfer, and the control matrix is the analogue.
